nodes.label: NVIDIA
nodes.subtitle: NVDA
nodes.description: Leading AI GPU designer. Blackwell and Hopper accelerators drive datacenter revenue. Depends on TSMC for leading-edge fabrication and SK Hynix/Samsung for HBM.

nodes.label: TSMC
nodes.subtitle: TSM
nodes.description: World's largest pure-play foundry. Manufactures NVIDIA, Apple, and AMD leading-edge chips. CoWoS advanced packaging is a key AI bottleneck.

nodes.label: ASML
nodes.subtitle: ASML
nodes.description: Monopoly supplier of EUV lithography scanners required for sub-7nm nodes. Equipment lead times directly constrain foundry capacity expansion.

nodes.label: SK Hynix
nodes.subtitle: 000660.KS
nodes.description: Primary HBM supplier for NVIDIA AI GPUs. First to mass-produce HBM3E. Memory fab capacity is a binding constraint on AI accelerator output.

nodes.label: Samsung Electronics
nodes.subtitle: 005930.KS
nodes.description: Competes in memory (HBM, DRAM) and foundry. Secondary HBM and CoWoS packaging supplier. EUV-enabled logic fabs in Pyeongtaek.

nodes.label: AMD
nodes.subtitle: AMD
nodes.description: Fabless CPU and GPU designer competing with NVIDIA in AI accelerators. Also depends on TSMC and HBM supply chain.

nodes.label: Amkor Technology
nodes.subtitle: AMKR
nodes.description: OSAT provider for advanced packaging including 2.5D interposer assembly, complementing TSMC CoWoS capacity.

nodes.label: HBM3E
nodes.description: Fifth-generation High Bandwidth Memory stacking 12 DRAM dies with ~1.2 TB/s bandwidth per stack. Critical for AI training GPUs.

nodes.label: CoWoS
nodes.description: Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate — TSMC's 2.5D packaging integrating GPU die with HBM stacks on a silicon interposer. Lead time bottleneck for AI chips.

nodes.label: EUV Lithography
nodes.description: 13.5nm wavelength lithography enabling 5nm and below nodes. ASML is the sole equipment supplier; scanner delivery schedules gate fab ramps.

nodes.label: NVIDIA B200
nodes.description: Blackwell-generation AI GPU with 192GB HBM3E, manufactured on TSMC 4NP with CoWoS packaging. Primary demand driver for leading-edge capacity.

nodes.label: NVIDIA H100
nodes.description: Hopper-generation datacenter GPU. Established the HBM3 supply chain dependencies still affecting the industry.

nodes.label: Photolithography
nodes.description: Patterning process transferring circuit designs onto wafer photoresist. EUV variants required for sub-7nm layers.

nodes.label: Advanced Packaging
nodes.description: 2.5D/3D integration of multiple dies (CoWoS, InFO). Separates memory bandwidth scaling from logic node scaling for AI chips.

nodes.label: Memory Fabrication
nodes.description: DRAM wafer fabrication and die stacking for HBM. SK Hynix and Samsung dominate AI-grade HBM production.

nodes.label: AI Training
nodes.description: Large-scale model training workloads driving demand for highest-bandwidth GPUs, HBM, and datacenter power infrastructure.

nodes.label: Data Centers
nodes.description: Hyperscaler and enterprise datacenter buildouts. Primary deployment venue for AI accelerators; capex cycles amplify semiconductor demand.

nodes.label: Cloud AI Services
nodes.description: AWS, Azure, GCP AI compute rental. Cloud providers are largest buyers of NVIDIA accelerators, linking end demand to chip orders.

scenarios.name: AI Demand Surge
scenarios.description: Hyperscaler capex accelerates. NVIDIA B200 orders spike, straining TSMC CoWoS and HBM supply chains.

scenarios.name: HBM Shortage
scenarios.description: HBM3E supply fails to meet GPU demand. SK Hynix allocation becomes critical bottleneck for NVIDIA shipments.

scenarios.name: EUV Equipment Delays
scenarios.description: ASML scanner delivery delays push out TSMC and Samsung fab ramps, constraining leading-edge GPU output.

scenarios.name: CoWoS Capacity Expansion
scenarios.description: TSMC expands CoWoS packaging lines. Advanced packaging becomes gating factor for AI accelerator production.
